recreation_prompt_markdown:
Create a mobile-first arcade cooking game about running a neon snack stand for an excited crowd during a short, high-energy rush. The game should play in a single full-screen top-down kitchen scene drawn on an HTML canvas, with a vivid palette of purples, oranges, mint greens, and golds, plus flashy HUD panels and playful animated feedback. Frame the experience as a chef serving fans in a street-food lane or concert-side snack corridor, with a fun, upbeat, slightly chaotic tone instead of realistic simulation.

Use a simple touch-friendly control scheme: a virtual joystick on the lower left moves the chef freely around the kitchen floor, and one large action button on the lower right performs context-sensitive interactions. The player should never need multiple action buttons. Interaction should depend on proximity and what the chef is currently carrying.

Structure the kitchen clearly. Put customer positions along a counter at the top of the screen. Place ingredient crates on the left side, prep stations on the right side, and a trash bin near the bottom center for discarding mistakes. The chef can carry only one item at a time. Include two order lines: one for a burger and one for a salad. The burger path should be raw meat from a crate to a stove, then into a finished burger. The salad path should be lettuce from a crate to a prep board, then into a finished salad. When the chef interacts with a valid station while holding the matching raw ingredient, the item should be placed there and process over a short duration with a visible progress bar. Once complete, interacting again should pick up the final dish.

Make the session a 90-second score attack. Customers should spawn into up to three fixed slots along the top counter and each display a visible requested dish in a speech bubble. Every customer needs a patience bar that slowly drains while they wait. If patience reaches zero, that customer leaves and the player loses points. If the chef reaches a customer while holding the exact requested dish, the order is served successfully, the player gains points based on remaining patience, a small time bonus is added, and the customer disappears.

Build the game loop around fast route optimization: collect ingredients, start prep, move efficiently, pick up finished dishes, and serve the most urgent customer before they leave. Reward quick, correct service with juicy feedback such as hearts, coins, smoke puffs from cooking stations, short celebratory animation cards or GIF-like reactions, crisp UI sounds, a looping upbeat background track, and distinct serve, fail, blocked, and game-over sound cues.

Include a start screen with a bold arcade title, a short instruction line, and a simple chef-color selection that changes the player avatar palette. Show a compact HUD during play with score and remaining time. When time reaches zero, stop the action, display a game-over panel with the final score, and offer an immediate restart button. Keep the experience readable, responsive, and satisfying on phones, emphasizing short-session replayability over progression systems, story, or deep simulation.

identity.title: Chef Rush: Fan Fever
identity.premise: A neon-styled mobile arcade cooking game where a chef runs a hype-filled snack stand, preparing simple dishes for impatient fans before time runs out.
identity.interaction_model: Real-time top-down movement with a virtual joystick and a single context-sensitive action button for picking up ingredients, using stations, serving customers, and discarding mistakes.
identity.objective: Serve the correct burger or salad orders as quickly as possible to earn cheers, protect score, and stretch the session with small time bonuses.
identity.progression: A single-session score attack loop with rising queue pressure from repeatedly spawning customers, patience decay, and constant route optimization rather than level-based advancement.
identity.theme: Neon street-food stand, crowd energy, concert-lane fandom, playful chef performance.
identity.mood: Fast, upbeat, colorful, arcadey, and lightly chaotic.
identity.likely_audience: Players who enjoy casual mobile cooking games, short arcade score chases, and approachable one-button task loops.
confidence_notes: High confidence in the cooking-service loop because item, station, customer, score, and patience logic are explicit in code.
Moderate confidence in the exact branding/title because the HTML title and on-screen title differ slightly, but both point to the same snack-rush fan-service concept.

identity.recreation_prompt: Create a mobile-first arcade cooking game set in a neon street-food lane where the player controls a cheerful chef during a 90-second fan rush. Present the game in a top-down single-screen kitchen rendered on a full-screen canvas, with a bright neon-purple palette, flashy HUD, crowd-facing counter at the top, ingredient stations on the left and right, and large on-screen touch controls: a virtual joystick on the lower left and one large action button on the lower right. Start with a title screen where the player chooses a chef color, then begin a fast score-attack session. Customers appear in up to three fixed slots along the top counter and request either a burger or a salad, shown clearly in speech bubbles. Each customer has a patience meter that drains over time; if it empties, the customer leaves and the player loses points. The chef can carry only one item at a time. The core loop should be: grab meat from one crate or lettuce from another, take meat to a stove or lettuce to a prep board, wait for a short progress bar to complete, pick up the finished dish as burger or salad, then deliver it to the matching nearby customer. Let the action button be context-sensitive so it handles pickup, placement, collection, serving, and trashing wrong items based on proximity. Award score based on how much patience remains when serving, add a small time bonus for successful service, and end the game when the timer reaches zero. Include punchy sound feedback, celebratory particles, animated positive/negative reaction feedback, a clean score-and-timer HUD, and a game-over screen that shows final score and allows an immediate restart. The tone should feel playful, fast, accessible, and optimized for short touch-screen sessions rather than deep simulation.

The game simulates a reduced kitchen workflow with ingredient pickup, station processing, dish completion, and delivery, though in a simplified arcade form.
The game is not a narrative or systemic time-loop title, but it does revolve around a repeating short timed session where optimizing the same production cycle is the core structure.
There is light resource and throughput management through item carrying limits, station occupancy, customer patience, and movement routing.
The game includes tactile one-button interactions, progress bars, particles, sounds, and positive feedback that support a satisfying casual-play feel, though this is secondary to the cooking loop.
